is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.s. (Odumasy and Kisumu strains), page 1.

reports_target_markers.evidence: No primary genotyping of target resistance markers was conducted. The paper only mentions that the Odumasy strain has a high frequency (84%) of West African kdr (Vgsc L995F) based on previous literature (Yawson et al. 2004) and citing unpublished data that the laboratory colony is fixed for kdr (page 9).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies were generated or reported in this study; it is an expression profiling study using the detox microarray chip.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes used were colonized laboratory strains (Odumasy strain colonized in 2002 and laboratory-selected with permethrin; and Kisumu susceptible strain), page 9.

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary research article reporting microarray gene expression profiling in Anopheles gambiae.

sub_country_location.evidence: The Odumasy strain originated from Odumasy, Southern Ghana (page 8-9).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Specimens for the Odumasy colony were collected in 2002 (page 9).

supplement.evidence: Additional file 1 contains microarray transcript expression values, not field genotype frequencies.

assessment.summary: This study performs microarray expression profiling using the detox chip to identify metabolic resistance genes (such as CYP6M2 and CYP6Z2) upregulated in a colonized pyrethroid-resistant strain from Odumasy, Ghana, compared with the Kisumu strain. No field mosquito populations were genotyped for resistance markers.
exclusion_reasons: No target resistance markers were genotyped in this study.
No extractable field genotype frequency or count data reported.
Only colonized laboratory strains (Odumasy and Kisumu) were tested.
